title: Pauri 13: trusting, awareness
hook: mannai: by trust the mind becomes aware and knows all realms (Japji 13)
tomorrow: Pauri 14: trusting, the path is clear

segments.voice: Yesterday, gat: the state of the one who trusts can't be described. Your line was no pen for this. Today, what trusting does to the mind.

You'd think trust would make you sleepy: relax, you've got this, lean back. But watch a child on a parent's shoulders at a parade. Because she's safe up there, she sees everything: the drummers, the balloons, the dog in the crowd. The child on the ground, gripping a hand and worried about getting lost, sees knees. Safety doesn't dull her. It frees her attention to look around. Pauri 13 makes a claim like that: trusting doesn't put the mind to sleep. It wakes it up.
screen: `A CHILD ON A PARENT'S SHOULDERS.` → `SAFE, SO SHE SEES EVERYTHING.` → `TRUST WAKES THE MIND.`

segments.voice: Pauri 13 opens: mannai surat hovai man budh. By trusting, surat comes into the mind and the understanding. Surat, today's word, carries real weight in Sikh teaching: awareness, attention, consciousness, the part of you that's awake and noticing. In Sikh thought, surat is what attunes to the shabad, the Word, the way a radio tunes to a station. In the Sidh Gosht, Guru Nanak's dialogue with the yogis, the Word is called the Guru and the attentive mind, surat, the disciple. The pauri goes on, in paraphrase. By trusting, one knows of all the realms, every world. By trusting, one doesn't take blows to the face. By trusting, one doesn't go off with the messenger of death. And the refrain: such is the Name of the Stainless One, known only to the one who trusts it in the mind. Notice the order. Before knowing all realms, before escaping fear, the first gift of trust is that you wake up. Listening gave direction; trusting gives attention. It fits an ordinary Tuesday, too. When you're anxious, attention shrinks to one tight spot, the worry. When you trust, it opens: the light on the wall, the tone in someone's voice, what the moment is actually asking. One way to hear the blows to the face and the messenger of death is as the stanza's picture of fear; some commentators read them as what awaits after death. A mind that trusts doesn't flinch at every shadow. It has room to see.
screen: `MANNAI SURAT HOVAI MAN BUDH.` · `SURAT — AWARENESS, ATTENTION.` · `AWARENESS COMES FIRST.` · `FEAR SHRINKS, TRUST OPENS.` · then, large: `TRUST WAKES YOU.`

segments.voice: Let attention move slowly down your body, from the top of your head to your feet, just noticing, fixing nothing. Then feel the whole body at once, one shape, breathing, and rest there. If the mind narrows onto a worry, widen it again to the whole body.
Surat. Awareness, attention, the waking consciousness that tunes to the Word. By trusting, Pauri 13 says, surat comes.
Your line: trust wakes you. Safe on those shoulders, she saw the whole parade. See you tomorrow.
